transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Um... hi. Well, I guess... I've just been having some issues at work lately. I'm an auditor, and... I keep starting these follow-up items after my audits, or sometimes mentorship events. I always have every intention of finishing them. But... then I'll find out, days later, that the final email or the review note or form just... never actually got done. So... yeah. That's what pushed me to make the appointment.
Did these kinds of follow-through problems start when you were a child?

I guess so, yeah. Um... even in elementary school, my report cards usually said I was bright, but... I lost assignments a lot. Or I'd rush past details, talk out of turn... need reminders to finish things. My mom actually still jokes about it. She says I could ace a test but... completely forget to turn in the project that was sitting right there in my backpack. So... it's been a while, I suppose.
Did these attention and follow-through problems also happen at home or in other settings, not just at work or school?

Yeah, um... it's not just work. At home, it's... well, my husband basically handles all the bills now. And any commitments I agree to, he kind of has to take over because... he just can't really count on me to actually finish them. And at work, it's... it's getting worse. A client review got messed up because of my mistakes and the unfinished follow-ups. I just... I worry people are starting to question if I can even handle the promotion I'm up for. So, yeah. It's everywhere, really.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention when you need to focus on something, like reading a report or listening in a meeting?

Yes. Um... especially if it's long. Like, I can start a client meeting or one of those AI-tool trainings we have to do... and I'm fully engaged at first. But then... I don't know, my mind just kind of slips off. I'll realize later that I missed the last few minutes entirely, even though I was sitting right there, looking at the screen.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a lifelong pattern of inattention and poor follow-through beginning in childhood, occurring across settings (school, home, work), with current functional impairment at work and at home. Symptoms include losing assignments, missing details, talking out of turn, needing reminders, difficulty sustaining attention in meetings, and failing to complete tasks. This is most consistent with Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation.
